newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU soft wheat exports reach half last year's rate.
newsitem.headline: EU soft wheat exports reach half last year's rate.

text.p: European Union wheat exports have made up some of the ground lost on last year after active sales during the past month, EU figures showed on Monday.
Soft wheat exports approved by the European Commission amounted to 1.465 million tonnes on October 8, or just over half the amount marked down for export by the same date last year.
Exports have doubled since September 10, when the EU was at less than a third of its year-ago export rate.
Exports are measured in certificates delivered by the Commission starting on July 1.
The breakdown dated October 8 was distributed to the EU's cereals management committee on October 10 and supplied to Reuters by member-country grain officials.
On October 10, the committee additionally approved the export of 192,450 tonnes of soft wheat from the EU open market.
Wheat flour exports on October 8 were at 1.351 million tonnes, or 84 percent of their equivalent level in 1995.
France's cereals authority, ONIC, last week called on the EU to maximise wheat exports in coming months to avoid a possible dip in prices when southern hemisphere crops reach the market.
But the EU says it will not start dumping wheat abroad.
